title: MAGIC ENGLISH GRADE 7 — WORLD 7: C1 ADVANCED ACADEMIC & RESEARCH ENGLISH
description: An advanced academic world focused on research literacy, evidence, synthesis, critical interpretation, formal argument, and precise communication of complex ideas.

targets.vocabulary: 3900+ active words with academic, analytical, and research collocations
targets.reading: 2200–2800 words with synthesis, inference, evaluation, and source comparison
targets.listening: 22–28 minutes across lectures, seminars, interviews, and expert discussions
targets.speaking: 26–34 minutes of structured academic discussion, explanation, and defense
targets.writing: 800–1000 words across analytical essays, research summaries, and evidence-based arguments
targets.presentation: 13–17 minutes with visual explanation, synthesis, and live questioning
targets.researchCommunication: clear C1 communication of evidence, uncertainty, interpretation, and conclusions

grammar: advanced nominalization and information-dense academic structures
complex passive and reporting constructions for source attribution
modal verbs and modal perfects for evidence, probability, and cautious claims
advanced conditionals for hypotheses, limitations, and counterfactual analysis
participial and reduced clauses for concise formal writing
inversion, fronting, clefting, and emphasis in formal argument
advanced relative clauses, apposition, and embedded structures
cohesion through reference, substitution, lexical chains, and discourse markers
hedging, boosting, concession, qualification, and epistemic stance
register control across academic, research, seminar, and public-facing communication

missions.title: Academic Vocabulary Forge
missions.focus: Academic word families, collocations, nominalization, and precise lexical choice
missions.outcome: Use sophisticated academic vocabulary accurately rather than relying on vague general words.

missions.title: Research Question Architect
missions.focus: Turning broad topics into focused, answerable research questions
missions.outcome: Formulate precise questions that define scope, variables, context, and purpose.

missions.title: Evidence Detective
missions.focus: Claims, evidence, examples, limitations, and source reliability
missions.outcome: Distinguish strong support from weak, irrelevant, or insufficient evidence.

missions.title: Inference & Interpretation Lab
missions.focus: Reading implications, assumptions, patterns, and unstated conclusions
missions.outcome: Make careful inferences while separating what a source states from what it suggests.

missions.title: Source Reporting Mastery
missions.focus: Attribution verbs, reporting structures, paraphrase, and source integration
missions.outcome: Report ideas from sources accurately while maintaining an appropriate academic register.

missions.title: Paraphrase Precision Lab
missions.focus: Meaning preservation, structural transformation, and lexical flexibility
missions.outcome: Paraphrase complex information without distorting meaning or overusing source wording.

missions.title: Synthesis Engine
missions.focus: Combining multiple sources into a coherent analytical position
missions.outcome: Connect, compare, and synthesize sources instead of summarizing them separately.

missions.title: Argument Architecture
missions.focus: Thesis, claims, reasons, evidence, counterarguments, and conclusions
missions.outcome: Build logically connected arguments that remain clear across complex ideas.

missions.title: Bias & Framing Intelligence
missions.focus: Loaded language, framing, omission, perspective, and rhetorical positioning
missions.outcome: Identify how language choices can influence interpretation without confusing framing with evidence.

missions.title: Academic Seminar Arena
missions.focus: Turn-taking, clarification, challenge, qualification, and evidence-based response
missions.outcome: Participate actively in advanced seminar discussion while developing ideas spontaneously.

missions.title: Comparative Research Reading
missions.focus: Comparing methodology, claims, findings, limitations, and conclusions across texts
missions.outcome: Evaluate similarities and differences between complex sources with precision.

missions.title: Lecture & Expert Listening Lab
missions.focus: Following extended explanations, signposting, examples, qualifications, and conclusions
missions.outcome: Extract structure, key evidence, and speaker stance from demanding academic speech.

missions.title: Analytical Essay Mission
missions.focus: Thesis development, paragraph logic, evidence integration, and synthesis
missions.outcome: Write a coherent C1 analytical essay with a defensible central argument.

missions.title: Research Summary Workshop
missions.focus: Abstract-style compression, findings, limitations, and implications
missions.outcome: Reduce complex research into a concise and accurate professional summary.

missions.title: Academic Presentation Lab
missions.focus: Explaining research, interpreting visuals, signposting, and answering questions
missions.outcome: Present complex information clearly to an audience with different levels of expertise.

missions.title: Methodology & Limitations Mission
missions.focus: Methods, variables, uncertainty, limitations, and cautious interpretation
missions.outcome: Discuss how research design affects the strength and scope of conclusions.

missions.title: Science, Technology & Society Research
missions.focus: Interdisciplinary evidence, public impact, ethics, and competing interpretations
missions.outcome: Discuss complex science-and-society questions using evidence and qualified claims.

missions.title: Research Conference Simulation
missions.focus: Poster-style explanation, peer questions, critique, response, and revision
missions.outcome: Defend an idea professionally while responding constructively to critical questions.

missions.title: World 7 Integrated Research Marathon
missions.focus: Integrated reading, listening, source analysis, discussion, writing, and presentation
missions.outcome: Complete a multi-stage research communication challenge using sustained C1 English.

missions.title: WORLD 7 MASTER QUEST — C1 ADVANCED ACADEMIC & RESEARCH ENGLISH
missions.focus: End-to-end research communication from question to evidence, synthesis, argument, and presentation
missions.outcome: Demonstrate independent C1 academic communication through a complete research-style mission.

realWorldScenarios: Choosing a focused research question for a school or personal project
Comparing two sources that reach different conclusions
Explaining why evidence supports one interpretation more strongly than another
Summarizing a complex article for someone who has not read it
Participating in a seminar and responding to a challenging question
Presenting research findings with charts or other visual evidence
Explaining research limitations without undermining the entire project
Writing an evidence-based recommendation for a real-world problem
Defending a research interpretation during a conference-style Q&A
Communicating complex research findings to a general audience

assessment.successCriteria: Learner can independently interpret, compare, synthesize, and communicate complex information in clear C1 academic English while distinguishing evidence, inference, uncertainty, and personal interpretation.
